messages:
support: FYI — customer 'BrightSky' (acct BSK-42) opened a high-sev about p99 jumping ~3x over the last deploy. They report interactive latency for short prompts spiking to 1.2s. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BSK-7891 :rotating_light:

natalie: Thanks. Is this only small prompts or all traffic? Any error rates?

support: Only small prompts (< 64 tokens). No 5xxs. Throughput normal. p50/p95 stable, p99 bad. Happened ~2026-03-10 18:10 UTC right after continuous-batcher config rollout to prod.

mike: grabbing metrics now. Running quick PromQL for tail by prompt_length.

mike: promql -> sum by (tenant, prompt_bucket) (histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))) | shows BSK tenants with p99 spike on bucket "<64" from ~0.28 -> ~1.1s around 1762978000.

cheng: looking at config diff from that rollout. I pulled the staged config that was promoted. Key changes below:
```diff
- continuous_batcher:
-   small_batch_timeout_ms: 30
-   grace_window_ms: 20
+ continuous_batcher:
+   small_batch_timeout_ms: 200
+   grace_window_ms: 100
+   tiny_request_policy: coalesce
```
This increases the hold time massively for tiny payloads.

natalie: That aligns with symptom: raising small_batch_timeout -> longer tail for low-concurrency tiny requests. Why was this change made?

cheng: It was from the 'microburst smoothing' tuning PR — intended to reduce throughput jitter for medium-sized batches, but the rollout forgot to include per-tenant overrides for tiny_request_policy. The default now forces coalescing tiny requests instead of bypassing.

ops: Got a reproducer locally using the curl loop for short prompts. Steps:
1) curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16}' | jq -r .latency
2) run k=100 concurrent loops spaced 10ms
Observed median ~55ms, p99 ~1.05s when continuous-batcher config hex is applied.

mike: Can we patch to reduce the hold for tiny payloads per-tenant as a quick mitigation? e.g., set small_batch_timeout_ms: 25 for tenants flagged as tiny-sensitive.

natalie: Yes. We should do a per-tenant override for BSK-42 and any others with similar profiles, and roll back the global default to previous values. Quick plan:
- apply per-tenant override (small_batch_timeout_ms=25, tiny_request_policy: bypass) for BSK-42 (owner: cheng)
- revert global rollout to small_batch_timeout_ms=30, grace_window_ms=20 (owner: mike)
- run canary for 30m and monitor p99 (owner: natalie)

cheng: I'll push the override now. Patch payload to config service: 
```json
{"tenant_id":"BSK-42","overrides":{"continuous_batcher":{"small_batch_timeout_ms":25,"tiny_request_policy":"bypass"}}}
```

deploy-bot: Started config update for tenant BSK-42 (change id cfg-2026-03-10-002). Rolling out to 3 nodes.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete to 3/3 nodes (cfg-2026-03-10-002) :white_check_mark:

ops: Re-ran the local reproducer against tenant override. p99 dropped from ~1.05s to ~0.18s. Customer bumped to green for p99; p95 unchanged.

mike: I'll open a rollback PR for the global default and pin the canary. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4567

natalie: Great. After rollback and tenant overrides are live, we should add a test in the perf-suite that fuzzes continuous-batcher parameters against <64 token traffic to catch regressions. Also add a /playbook entry under runbooks/continuous-batching for per-tenant overrides and quick mitigations.

support: Filed a post-update for the customer and linked ticket. Customer confirmed better p99 in a few tests.

cheng: Note for followup — we need to update rollout checklist: require validation matrix that includes "tiny prompt latency" and a per-tenant opt-out flag. I'll add that to the rollout PR template.

natalie: Assigned owners: cheng (tenant override & rollout checklist), mike (global rollback PR), ops (repro steps + perf test). We'll reconvene if metrics don't stabilize in 2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

support: Thanks team — I'll keep the customer looped in. :thumbsup:
